scope: Experimental local two-fleet stopped Docker recovery with one native Void cron app and an opt-in queue survivor; ordinary cron admission remains closed

a.coldRowFingerprintBasis: One row fingerprint matched against the live pre-pause source sample and two independent restored cold queries; final postflight compares stopped source volume bytes with the archives.
a.controllerRunningHoldRowBasis: Fingerprint-pinned driver compares the complete source rows before and after the held interval; only its final native control is stored in the raw runningHold record.

fate.outcome: pause clears retry identity; separate resume schedules future work
fate.oldRowsValidationBasis: Executed assertNoReplay compares all attempts, results and occurrence counters through resume requestedAt-1; the complete post-resume tables are not stored in this raw record.

olderLoss.olderCase: due-timer snapshot A, before pending-retry snapshot B
olderLoss.notice: Pausing clears pending timer and retry identity. Resume schedules a future occurrence; unfinished work is not a retained backlog. An older snapshot can lose acknowledged results or replay external effects. Reconcile application records before acknowledging.
olderLoss.afterBForkNote: B-branch attempts are absent in older A; they were created after forking the B restore and were never part of the A archive.

limits: Same-version local Docker profile with preserved identities and all volumes; no live snapshot or topology transformation
Older case restores due-timer snapshot A from before retry snapshot B
Pausing clears timer/retry identity; no retained missed-tick backlog or arbitrary external-effect exactly-once guarantee

Scoped cron admission, retirement beside another live cron, native CPU exhaustion, upstream Rust test execution and release-bound runtime qualification remain open; cron/queue retirement has separate bounded evidence

queuedSurvivor.completionVerification: GET only after acknowledgment and separate resume; no input resubmission

assertionBasis: Cold source/before/after rows, queued snapshot state, selected future rows, source/target approval pins and archive hashes are independently checked by the curator. Runtime operations, warm-hold row comparisons, paused route/resume refusals and old-ledger checks after resume are assertions in the fingerprint-pinned driver whose terminal exit0 was independently observed. Row fingerprints cover retained private data; manifest identifiers cover full private manifests rather than their public projections. Postflight independently reads stopped volumes and compares both original sources after the entire drill.
